analysis:
Examined the changed hunks in ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift and ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift, plus the surrounding load and unload code.

ModelLoading changes: unloadModel now calls selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now: .now) on the Nemotron Super retirement path (lines 1133-1137) and at the end of a normal unload (line 1203). This only schedules an earlier recheck of waiting selected models at the next capacity tick. It adds no new data path, no new trust decision and no authorization change. Resource cleanup order is unchanged: engineV2Runtime.unregister, GLM5NextRetirement.beforeRelease, releaseAssistant, container release, slot removal, clearCache, then regrow of survivors. The unproven-retirement early return (lines 1157-1164) is untouched.

The load path (lines 552-1037) is unchanged context. It retains the TOCTOU weight-hash bracketing, with a fresh cryptographic hash required for reusable SSD cache participation. That keeps T-041 and T-012/T-027 behavior as before. The cache-eligible hash is passed only when the verified artifact hash is available. Nothing in the diff touches the SSD cache, the KEK, the lookup tags or the TTL.

ModelSelection changes: enabledModelsAtLastSwitch is set when a model replacement is staged and restored in the rollback path alongside hasPersistedModelSwitch. The state transitions are symmetric. Only the diff hunks were visible, so I could not confirm that enabledModelsAtLastSwitch is consumed safely elsewhere. That filter should not widen the advertised or served model set beyond the persisted selection.

No security regression was identified in the supplied evidence. Remaining integration questions: where enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery are consumed (ProviderLoop state definitions are outside this batch), and whether makeAllDue can trigger load storms. That is an availability concern only, and it is bounded by the existing load gate.
